howDoI.q: How do I draw a room that looks as if it is seen from a corner?
How do I make a cube that has a top and two sides?
How do I make a wall that runs on a slant?
How do I draw a tower that is taller than one block?
How do I make steps that look as if they climb?
How do I make an arrow key walk on a slant?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Corner View is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short rooms, all drawn as if you were looking at them from one corner: a floor of diamonds, cubes with a top and two sides, a stair of towers and a floor shaped like a diamond. It takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

The four arrows walk Kit: the squares in the first two rooms, the diagonals in the third. Space does nothing. Walk onto the gold diamond to go on. Nothing in this game hurts Kit.

pages.head: Level 1: The Corner Room
pages.html:
Level 1: The Corner Room

Kit starts on the green diamond in the middle of a room of cubes. The DIAMOND FLOOR, SQUARE GRID sign says what this is: the floor is drawn in diamonds, but the game under it is still squares. The A CUBE IS ONE BLOCK sign points at the cubes: each one is a diamond top and two sides, in a single 20 by 20 block.

A wall of cubes climbs to the right, like a wall seen from a corner. Walk straight at it and Kit is stopped. The ARROWS WALK THE SQUARES sign says why: here each arrow is one straight square step, even though Kit is drawn facing a diagonal. Level 3 shows how to make a diagonal step. He goes up one, right one, up one, right one, round the open top end of the wall, and down to the gold diamond.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • One picture, cut into blocks. The floor, the cubes, the signs' posts and the two diamonds were painted as one 320 by 200 picture and cut into 20 by 20 blocks. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor to see them. The floor's diamonds repeat every 20 pixels, so every plain floor cell comes out as the same block, which is why a whole room needs few blocks.
  • A cube is one block. A cube is 20 pixels wide and 20 tall: a diamond top, a left side in a darker color and a right side darker still. The cube blocks have Solid sides checked, so Kit cannot walk through them. Their four corners show the floor.
  • The wall that runs on a slant. Open one.map in the map editor. The wall is cubes in cells that touch only at their corners, one row up and one column right each time. Kit moves a whole block at a time along the squares, so he cannot slip between two cubes that only touch at a corner. He goes up, then right, then up, then right.
  • The walls round the room. A ring of purple cubes closes the room in, and the whole map outside it is the same cube, so he never stops at something he cannot see.
  • Kit's place. He starts in the middle of the screen on purpose: the view is fixed, and the game centers it on where he starts. Open cv.gam in the scenes editor: its scroll settings are all off, so the picture stays put.
  • Kit in a corner view. Open square.chr in the character editor. Every block in this game has Gravity pulls unchecked, and Kit has four walks and no jump. His pictures (kit.cbl) face only the four diagonals, as a person seen from a corner, never the camera: facing front he would look wider than he is tall. Here each arrow still walks one square step, so Up faces upper right while moving straight up. Level 3 fixes that.

What it cannot do. A corner view is a picture, not a 3D room. The game cannot sort what is in front from what is behind, so Kit is always drawn on top of everything: he cannot walk behind a cube or a tower. And his moves stay square: in these two rooms he cannot walk along the drawn diagonal, only up, down, left and right. Level 3 does.

pages.head: Level 2: Stairs of Towers
pages.html:
Level 2: Stairs of Towers

Kit starts on the green diamond in the middle again, and the gold diamond is on the far side of a stair of five towers: one, two and three blocks tall, and back down. The TALL TOWERS COVER THE BLOCKS ABOVE THEM sign says what a tall tower is: its picture covers the block above the one it stands on, so that block is solid too.

Walk left and the stair stops him. Go right past its end, down, along the front and up to the gold diamond. The KIT IS ALWAYS IN FRONT sign is about him: he is drawn over everything, so he never goes behind a tower.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A tall tower is more than one block. A cube is 20 pixels tall. A tower that rises further is a taller picture: the top diamond sits in the block above the one it stands on. Open two.bbl: the three-block tower is the top, the middle and the bottom blocks of one painting, and each has Solid sides checked. The blocks above a tower's foot are solid too, because the tower's picture is drawn there and Kit should not be able to stand on it.
  • The stair is only a picture. The towers are one, two and three blocks tall, lined up in a row, so they look like steps. Kit does not climb them: they are walls, and he walks round them.
  • Kit is in front. The game draws Kit over every block. A game that sorts by depth would draw a tower over him when he walks behind it. Here the picture would have to be changed by hand: each tower would need a second set of blocks, put in place when Kit passes. That is a good next step to try.

What it cannot do. There is no real depth sorting, and Kit's walks stay square here. Everything else is the same game as level 1.

pages.head: Level 3: The Diamond Floor
pages.html:
Level 3: The Diamond Floor

The room is a diamond, and every arrow walks along one of its edges. Kit is drawn facing the way he walks, always one of the four slants and never the camera. Four signs in the dark corners say which arrow goes where: UP: UPPER RIGHT, RIGHT: LOWER RIGHT, DOWN: LOWER LEFT, LEFT: UPPER LEFT. The EACH ARROW TAKES THE DIAGONAL NEAREST IT sign says why this fits: Up and Right lean toward the top and the right of the screen, so they take the slants nearest them, and the other two follow around.

To go straight right or left, tap two arrows in turn: Left, then Down, again and again, makes a straight line left; Up, then Right, makes one to the right. Walk into the lower right wall with Right, then hold Up all the way to the gold diamond.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A step that moves both ways. Open diag.chr in the character editor and look at the Up sequence. Each frame has an X of 4 and a Y of -2: the engine adds both to his place on every frame, so one key walks a slant. The floor's diamonds are twice as wide as tall, so a step along their edge is 4 across and 2 up or down. square.chr, used in levels 1 and 2, has an X or a Y but never both.
  • The same pictures. Both character files use kit.cbl: four slants, three poses each (a step, standing, the other step). The left-hand ones are the right-hand ones mirrored.
  • Which arrow goes where. Up is upper right, Right is lower right, Down is lower left and Left is upper left: each arrow takes the slant nearest its own direction, going around clockwise, so the four still feel like the four arrows. A sequence is tied to a key, so you can pick any mapping.
  • A wall on a slant. Open three.map. The diamond's edges are cubes in steps of two blocks across and one down, the slope Kit walks. The blocks outside them are dark and solid. The engine moves him across, then down, and stops each at a solid block, so he glides along a slanted wall instead of sticking in it.

What it cannot do. Kit's box is still a square block, so his edges do not follow the diamond: he slides along a slanted wall in tiny steps, and he cannot stand on a diamond tile's exact corner. Straight up, down, left and right take two arrows in turn. Each level has one character file, so the arrows mean the same thing all through a level.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In one.map, move a cube of the wall one block and see where Kit can go.
  • Open a cube block in one.bbl and uncheck Solid sides: Kit walks right through the cube, drawn under him.
  • Change the colors of a cube's sides in the blocks editor.
  • Draw a new cube in a free block and put it in the map.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.
